title: Romeo and Juliet: Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Step into the streets of Verona, where an ancient grudge breaks to new mutiny and two star-crossed lovers meet their fate.
meta_desc: Foundations of Edexcel Romeo and Juliet: setting, characters, key themes, and the play's tragic structure.
final_note: You now know the bones of the tragedy. Next, you'll apply this to scenes and quotations.

concepts.def: Doomed by fate; the Prologue marks the lovers' destiny.
The bitter quarrel between Capulets and Montagues.
A sonnet that opens the play and reveals the ending.
A drama ending in catastrophe, often a hero's death.
A character whose traits contrast another's, e.g. Mercutio.
Male-led society; Lord Capulet rules the household.

walkthroughs.body_html: The play opens in Verona, a city torn by an 'ancient grudge' between two noble houses, the Capulets and the Montagues. Shakespeare uses the public brawl in Act 1 Scene 1 to show how the feud poisons every level of society, from the servants to Prince Escalus himself.

The Chorus's Prologue tells us in sonnet form that Romeo and Juliet are 'star-crossed' and 'take their life'. This shapes our reading: every meeting is shadowed by fate. Their first encounter at the Capulet ball is itself a shared sonnet.

The play follows a five-act tragic arc: love blooms (Acts 1-2), marriage and crisis (Act 3 with Mercutio and Tybalt's deaths), banishment (Act 4), and catastrophe in the Capulet tomb (Act 5). Each act tightens the noose of fate.
